agents.name: aid-auditor
agents.description: Read-only reviewer for PRD compliance. It holds the diff against the governing PRD's sections so every described behaviour is present and correct, judges a PRD against the code from aid-explorer's behaviour-to-code map, and runs the challenge's grounding lens. Use it at review gates, when a PRD-against-code check has to be independent, or when a PRD is being challenged.

agents.name: aid-craftsman
agents.description: Complex refinement. It takes a working first pass and makes it finished, with hard polish, deep cleanup, edge cases, performance, error handling, and coherence across many files, while preserving behaviour that already works. Use it after a first pass exists and needs to become production quality; not for greenfield first drafts.

agents.name: aid-creator
agents.description: First-pass creative work. It produces the first version of something new (drafts, copy, prototypes, sketches, scaffolds, an initial implementation of a fresh idea), quickly and clearly marked as a first pass for refinement. Use it to get a concrete starting point on the table; not for final polish or high-risk work.

agents.name: aid-designer
agents.description: Visual and UX direction. It defines flows, layout, interaction, information hierarchy, and visual language, writes them as direction others can build from, and reviews built UI against that direction. Use it before building UI, when a UX question needs a call, or to review a UI change; not for writing production code.

agents.name: aid-explorer
agents.description: Read-only research specialist. It answers a narrow question by reading code, branches, PRDs, plans, reference docs, and the web, and returns evidence-backed findings, not file dumps. It also produces the PRD-to-code map (each described behaviour mapped to the code that implements it, or a search trail) that curation, the grounding lens, and completion gates judge from. Use it for "where is X", "what do these branches and plans say about Y", comparing options, and gathering context before a Think or Make step.

agents.name: aid-inspector
agents.description: Read-only reviewer for code quality. It judges the diff as code, knowing no intent: correctness, safety, resources, concurrency, interface contracts, and test quality, carrying the bug-class checklist and hunting weakened proof. Use it at review gates, and on a single risky task's diff before the gate.

agents.name: aid-mechanic
agents.description: Technical builder for well-specified work. It implements features, tests, wiring, and refactors from a clear brief, verifies with captured evidence, and stops on any mismatch instead of improvising. Use it for routine implementation once the design is settled; not for open design questions or high-risk work.

agents.name: aid-navigator
agents.description: Read-only reviewer for goal drift. It holds the built result against the PRD's overview and goals, so what was built taken as a whole still serves what the PRD set out to do, and runs the challenge's goals lens. Use it at review gates, or when a PRD's goals are being challenged.

agents.name: aid-oracle
agents.description: Senior engineer for high-risk work. It implements novel or dangerous changes (concurrency, security, data migration, core algorithms, irreversible operations). Use it when being wrong is expensive.

agents.name: aid-sage
agents.description: Principal architect for architecture that crosses more than one project, the hardest problems no other role could settle, and the PRD review before work is called done. It weighs options against established principles, gives one recommendation with its trade-offs, and lands architecture as PRD fragments; when settling a design needs code, it builds that piece under the normal proof rules. Use it sparingly, on the orchestrator's judgement, never as a default step; architecture inside one project belongs to aid-oracle.

agents.name: aid-skeptic
agents.description: Read-only adversarial reviewer. It gets the diff, or the PRD alone, and assumes the change is broken: it hunts the concrete failure scenarios intent-aware reviewers forgive, and the PRD's contradictions, in its own context. Use it at review gates for fresh eyes, or when a PRD is being challenged.
